_contract: The Phase-C1 INSTANCE data the authorization assembler needs: which committed objects to read, which money figures to refuse a mis-priced session against, and what the session's stage conditions say. Every value here was a literal inside src/aadistill until 2026-09-08. Moving it out is what lets the core be reused by another experiment. AUTHORIZES NOTHING: this is configuration, not a grant.

accepted_pricing._why_restated: so a mis-priced session is REFUSED rather than mirrored. A ceiling that only echoes its source is not an independent check, and this is the last place a mis-priced session can be stopped before a grant exists. Amended 2026-09-04 for the approved repricing to the secure L40S rate of $1.09/h; every minute assumption is unchanged. The superseded triple at $0.99/h was 13.7578 / 12.2070 / 13.4277.
accepted_pricing._cap_amendment: 2026-09-11: the PROJECT cumulative cap rose from 283.76 to 320.00 (+36.24) with the approved execution package below. The per-attempt ceiling did NOT move and no minute assumption changed. The issuer refuses a grant naming any other cap, which is why this value lives here rather than being inferred from the ledger.

execution_package._contract: The maintainer decision this experiment's attempts run under. INSTANCE POLICY, which is why it is configuration and not core: the core knows nothing about attempts, packages, dollars or retries. AUTHORIZES NOTHING BY ITSELF -- a launch still needs a grant, an authorization, a launch-bound readiness record and a bundle.
execution_package.approved_by: maintainer decision, 2026-09-11, after independent engineering review of 55bb324a..199711af
execution_package.limits_do_not_transfer: the engineering allowance, the per-attempt ceiling, the attempt count, the package total and the project cap bind SEPARATELY. A cheap failure does not buy a fourth attempt; an unspent engineering allowance does not raise the per-attempt ceiling; the margin is for real accounting corrections and is not spendable.

attempt_counting.rule: invoking the formal launcher under a NEW one-use authorization consumes one formal attempt, even if it then refuses at $0 before any provider resource exists.
attempt_counting.not_counted: read-only checks, code repair and GPU engineering validation before an authorization is issued.
attempt_counting.prospective_only: this rule governs THIS package. It does not rewrite the 2026-09-04 ruling, under which attempt 3 was not consumed because no provider resource was created; that record stands verbatim as the rule its own attempt ran under.
attempt_counting.no_hidden_retries: one provider-create call and one resource per formal invocation. A replacement pod, an internal redraw, a fresh run_id or a re-issuance does not evade the count.

autonomous_formal_retry_requires_all_of: it can be CONFIRMED that no formal probe training has started
the failure is an ordinary infrastructure failure whose cause is identified and addressed
frozen science, the input contracts and the decision rule are unchanged
the previous resource is confirmed no longer billing
the remaining attempt count and package balance still fund a complete attempt plus teardown
the new attempt uses a new run identity and a complete, valid one-use authorization chain
stop_and_report: the first probe has STARTED training, whether or not it finished -- preserve all evidence and stop
it cannot be confirmed whether training started; absence of confirmation is not confirmation of absence
a real replay mismatch at stage D or E
an input-identity conflict that cannot be restored to the frozen binding
anything requiring a change to the scientific protocol
any complete, valid GO / NO-GO / INCONCLUSIVE -- all three end the package's formal attempts, and an INCONCLUSIVE is a result, never an engineering failure to spend past
a package, count, ceiling or cap boundary is reached, or a resource's billing state is unknown
never: re-running a valid INCONCLUSIVE in pursuit of a GO
changing arms, seeds, recipe, battery, statistics or the behavioural vetoes
engineering_allowance_does_not_authorize: consuming the frozen confirmation battery for an endpoint
a formal retry -- those come from this package's attempt count, not from the engineering allowance

stage_conditions.replay: stop before any recovery training on a parent or incumbent digest mismatch; preserve the evidence and treat it as the attempt's result
stage_conditions.device_handoff: stop before recovery if the card is not released
stage_conditions.training: all six trainings must complete before any evaluation; a training failure is C1_INCOMPLETE, not a partial confirmation experiment
stage_conditions.generation_admission: no probe is scored unless the generation protocol observed from its own raw summaries is comparable to the attested C1 protocol
stage_conditions.decision: stage I requires six complete admitted and scored probes
stage_conditions.retry: THIS authorization permits exactly one launch attempt and no automatic retry, no replacement pod and no ceiling increase. Whether a FURTHER attempt may be authorized is the execution package's question, not this artifact's: see execution_package.autonomous_formal_retry_requires_all_of.

one_use: ONE grant, ONE issuance, ONE launch attempt, ONE provider resource. A failure is this attempt's result. Unchanged by the 2026-09-11 package: the package does not make an authorization reusable, it states how many separate one-use chains may be issued and under exactly what conditions.
